name: Events planned in three places
summary: Brings event enquiries from the inbox onto one list, checks the venue calendar for each requested date, holds a free date with no guests invited, and drafts the reply in the enquiry's thread, so the inbox, the calendar and the event record agree. Crons read and draft; a person approves every reply before it is sent.

covered_by.enquiry-intake: intake cron (enquiry emails onto one list)
covered_by.qualify: skill (group size and date against the venue's rules, judged by hand)
covered_by.menu-and-quote: skill (set menus and dietary versions: no mapped platform)
covered_by.record-keeping: check cron (calendar hold with no guests invited, reply draft in the enquiry thread)

crons.name: intake
crons.summary: New enquiry emails from the enquiries label go onto one list (sender, subject and threading headers only).

crons.name: check
crons.summary: For each enquiry with booking details: hold a free date on the venue calendar, draft the reply in the thread, and queue its send for approval. Busy dates are marked Clash.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: reads of the enquiry label and the venue calendar, a reply draft in the enquiry's own thread, and a calendar hold with no guests invited. Sending a reply waits for a person.

google-workspace.covers: enquiry email list and headers, calendar free-busy checks and holds with no guests, reply drafts in the thread, reply sends (approval only)

gaps: Typeform is not built: the mining run has no Typeform platform evidence for this workflow, so enquiries arrive by Gmail only.
Microsoft 365: the mined pages hold no event or booking content and no kit operation covers events, so Outlook is not built.
Roller has no platform in the kit (core/sdk/platforms/roller is absent), so Roller bookings cannot be read or changed.
Menus, set-menu choices and dietary versions (menu-and-quote) have no mapped platform, so they stay a judgment step.

Entering the booking details (date, times, guest count) for each enquiry needs a screen in the CRM shell: nothing writes the bookings namespace yet. Until it exists, the agent or a person writes it into the store.
A rejected reply leaves its calendar hold in place. Moving or removing a hold needs calendar.events.patch or calendar.events.delete as live operations, which this build does not include.
Deposits, contracts, supplier bookings, staffing, run sheets, final numbers, event-day check-in and invoicing are not covered: no mapped platform describes them in the docs given.
Calendar free-busy is a read sent as a POST, but the kit labels the operation as a write, so the deploy needs KIT_ALLOW_WRITES=1 for the check cron to read the calendar.
The Google adapter is docs-only: its field names come from Google's Gmail and Calendar specs, and it has not run against a real Google Workspace account.
